origins: Pain without explanation can feel pointless, and nothing seems to come from it. The inability to see any good makes it worse.
teaches: “We also rejoice in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope.” “We know that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him, who are called according to His purpose.” “After you have suffered for a little while, the God of all grace… will Himself restore you, secure you, strengthen you, and establish you.” We may not see the reason now, but meaning can be found: comfort for others, deeper trust, and hope of restoration. “So we fix our eyes not on what is seen, but on what is unseen.”
self_statements: I get nothing out of this.
errors: Believing suffering is either useful or meaningless.
Predicting that no good will come.
Feeling pain and concluding that it is pointless.
questions: What have I learned or become through this, even small things?
Whom has my suffering made me more sensitive to?
What does Scripture say about God’s purposes?
What good could God bring, even if I cannot see it?
What would it mean to wait for meaning?
How could I use what I am learning to help someone?
truth: God can bring meaning from suffering, and nothing is wasted in His hands. I may not see it now, but I can look for growth, comfort for others, and hope of restoration.
hw_truths: God works all things for good.
He comforts me so I can comfort others.
log: Each month, note one thing suffering has taught you.
actions: Use your experience to encourage another.
prayer: Lord, I cannot see the meaning in this. Bring good from my pain, use me to comfort others, and hold me in hope. Amen.
